read.sections.0.text.source: The environment is everything around us: land, water, air, plants and animals. Environments change over time. As the climate changes, some places now get heavier rain, while others have longer dry seasons. People change places too. For example, when many trees are cut down on a hillside, heavy rain can wash the soil away more easily, because there are no roots to hold it. In Brookside, heavier rain now sometimes covers the low footbridge. Children use the bridge to reach school, and traders use it to reach the market. The community needs a plan.
read.sections.0.text.back: The environment is everything around us: land, water, air, plants and animals. The environment changes over time. As the climate changes, some places now get heavier rain while others have longer dry seasons. People change places too. For example, when many trees on a hill are cut down, heavy rain can wash the topsoil away more easily, because there are no roots to hold the soil. In Brookside, heavier rain now sometimes floods the low footbridge. Children use this bridge to go to school, and traders use it to go to the market. So the community needs a plan.

Children use it to go to school. The town needs a plan.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: The environment is everything around us: land, water, air, plants and animals. The environment can change. Now some places get more rain. Some places get less rain. read.sections.1.text.note: Great Green Wall = กำแพงสีเขียวอันยิ่งใหญ่ (seen in Thai media, but not fixed); the source label keeps the English name in brackets. Mangrove trees = ป่าชายเลน. Bangladesh = บังกลาเทศ, Senegal = เซเนกัล, Djibouti = จิบูตี (Royal Institute spellings, please confirm).
read.sections.1.text.source: Around the world, communities adapt to changes in their environment. In Bangladesh, many fields stay under water for months in the rainy season. Some farmers build floating gardens from water plants and grow vegetables on top. In Africa, countries from Senegal to Djibouti are working on the Great Green Wall. They plant trees and care for the land to stop it from turning into desert. On many coasts in Asia, people plant mangrove trees, whose roots help protect the shore from waves. Each of these is a response that fits the local place.
read.sections.1.text.back: Around the world, communities adapt to environmental change. In Bangladesh, many fields are under water for months in the rainy season. So some farmers build floating gardens from water plants and grow vegetables on top. In Africa, countries from Senegal to Djibouti are working together to build the Great Green Wall. They plant trees and care for the land so it doesn't turn into desert. Along many coasts in Asia, people plant mangrove forests, whose roots help protect the coast from waves. Each is a response that suits its local place.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: Communities around the world adapt. In Bangladesh, many fields are under water in the rainy season. So some farmers make gardens that float. They grow vegetables on top. In Africa, many countries plant trees across a wide, dry area. The trees help stop the land from turning into desert. In parts of Asia, people plant trees by the sea. The roots help keep the land safe from waves. Each response fits its place.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Communities around the world adapt. In Bangladesh, many fields go under water in the rainy season. So some farmers make gardens that can float. They grow vegetables on top. In Africa, many countries plant trees across a wide dry area. The trees help stop the land turning into desert. In parts of Asia, people plant trees by the sea. The roots help protect the land from waves. Each response suits its own place.

read.sections.2.text.note: wheelchair = รถเข็น and market cart = รถเข็นขายของ: both use รถเข็น, so the sentence says "คนที่ใช้รถเข็นหรือคนที่เข็นรถเข็นขายของ". Check it is not confusing; วีลแชร์ is an option for wheelchair. "phone or data" = โทรศัพท์หรืออินเทอร์เน็ต.
read.sections.2.text.source: A response only works if people can use it. Look at the three ideas for Brookside. A warning sign is quick, but it does not make the bridge safer, and some people cannot read it. Raising the bridge lowers the risk, and a ramp helps people who use wheelchairs or push carts. Phone alerts can warn people early, but not everyone has a phone or data. Printed notices at the market reach more people. Making sure that everyone can use a plan is called inclusion. Often, two ideas together work better than one, and it helps to ask the people who use the bridge.
read.sections.2.text.back: A response only works if people can use it. Look at the three ideas for Brookside. A warning sign is quick, but it doesn't make the bridge safer, and some people can't read signs. Raising the bridge reduces the risk, and ramps help people who use wheelchairs or people pushing market carts. Phone alerts tell people in advance, but not everyone has a phone or internet. Printed notices at the market reach more people. Making sure everyone can use a plan is called inclusion. Often two ideas together work better than one, and asking the people who use the bridge helps a lot.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: A plan only works if people can use it. A sign is quick. But it does not make the bridge safe. A higher bridge is safer. A ramp helps people who cannot use steps. A phone alert warns people early. But not everyone has a phone. Paper notices at the market help too. When everyone can use a plan, that is called inclusion. Two ideas together can work better than one.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: A plan only works if people can use it. A sign is quick, but doesn't make the bridge safe. A higher bridge is safer. A ramp helps people who can't use steps. A phone alert tells people early, but not everyone has a phone. Paper notices at the market help too. When everyone can use a plan, we call it inclusion. Two ideas together may work better than one.

watch.summary.source: In this short UNICEF video, people talk about climate change and disability. Heavy rain, landslides and storms can cause problems for a whole town. But the video says these events are even harder for children with disabilities. Not every child can hear a warning sound. Not every child can run to a safe place. So these children need different plans. The main message is to make these plans together, before danger comes. Ask people with disabilities, because they know what they need. The video asks for warnings that work for all, a safe path for all, and safe places that all can use. When you plan for everyone from the start, the plan is better for all.
watch.summary.back: In this short UNICEF video, people talk about climate change and disability. Heavy rain, landslides and storms can cause problems for a whole town. But the video says these events are even harder for children with disabilities. Not every child can hear a warning sound. Not every child can run to a safe place. So these children need different plans. The main message is to make these plans together before danger comes. Ask people with disabilities, because they know what they need. The video asks for warnings that work for everyone, safe routes for everyone and safe places everyone can use. When you plan for everyone from the start, the plan is better for everyone.
